title: Deriving Clinical Risk Tiers from Surgical Records: A Regression-Based Approach to the Surgery-Complication Risk Index (S-CRI)
content: Background: The identification of predictive biomarkers for surgical complications is essential for enhancing patient safety and optimizing hospital resources. While complex computational models offer strong predictive accuracy, there remains a critical clinical need for transparent, bedside-accessible biostatistical tools that operate without persistent computational infrastructure. Methods: Building upon our previously validated machine learning frameworks for surgical risk assessment, we conducted a retrospective analysis of 19,965 surgical patient records from Greek surgery departments. Univariate screening (Chi-squared and Mann-Whitney U tests) identified parameters robustly associated with complications. A multivariate logistic regression model was employed to calculate adjusted Odds Ratios (aOR). The resulting β-coefficients were converted into an integer point-based scoring system—the Surgery-Complication Risk Index (S-CRI)—by scaling all variables relative to the risk contribution of a single day of hospital stay. Model performance was validated using the Receiver Operating Characteristic (ROC) curve analysis. Results: Length of hospitality stay (OR 1.44 per day) and specific admission categories were identified as the strongest independent predictors. The finalized S-CRI incorporates a baseline offset (-3.1) alongside integer weights for stay duration, hospitality classification, and diagnostic risk groups. At an optimized clinical screening threshold of -4, the index achieved a sensitivity of 66.6%, a specificity of 89.6%, and an Area Under the Curve (AUC) of 0.882, matching the discriminative performance of advanced, high-dimensional computational models (Absolute Combined Model Accuracy: 86.52%). Conclusion: The S-CRI successfully collapses multi-layered statistical correlations into five transparent risk tiers, ranging from “Very Low” (<1% complication rate) to “Very High” (>75%). This tool provides a validated, zero-cost framework for clinical decision support, allowing surgical departments to deploy targeted monitoring protocols directly at the patient’s bedside without computational overhead.
